data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private companies and one public entity (277810.KQ) in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including near-stage and adjacent-stage peers such as Humanoid (Series A, $1.4B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next progression, implies a valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables—spanning Seed through Series B stages—yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects the wide valuation heterogeneity within the robotics and manufacturing sector at various stages.

Triangulation of both methods produces a working range of $42M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $850M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around growth trajectory and market timing relative to peers. Key drivers of valuation within this range include capital efficiency relative to peer burn rates, technical differentiation in manufacturing robotics, and path to near-term revenue inflection. Further diligence on go-to-market traction and unit economics would be needed to narrow this range materially.
